annotations.description: Chose to be on the draw in Modern. While the hand could benefit from an extra card to find a third artifact for Mox Opal's metalcraft, going first is almost always correct in Modern due to the significant tempo advantage. Being on the play would let them deploy Lavaspur Boots and potentially Emry a full turn earlier, and have Unholy Heat available to answer opponent's first threat before it can attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to let the opponent go first (be on the draw)
annotations.betterLine: Choose to go first. The tempo advantage in Modern generally outweighs the extra card, especially with interactive elements like Unholy Heat that benefit from being ahead on tempo.

annotations.description: Bottoming Cori-Steel Cutter weakens the Emry affinity plan. With both artifacts (Lavaspur Boots + Cori-Steel Cutter), the ideal line is T1 Boots, T2 Cutter + Emry for just U (affinity -2), then equip Boots for haste. This gives a very powerful turn 2. Without Cori-Steel Cutter, Emry costs 1U on T2 (only 1 artifact for affinity), which still works but is less efficient and leaves less mana open.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed Cori-Steel Cutter, keeping Unholy Heat
annotations.betterLine: Bottom Unholy Heat instead. The proactive artifact synergy plan (two cheap artifacts enabling a 1-mana Emry on T2 with haste from Boots) is stronger than keeping conditional removal. Emry's mill ability can find removal later.

annotations.description: When imprinting a card on Ugin's Labyrinth, the player chose World Breaker over Sire of Seven Deaths or Devourer of Destiny. World Breaker is arguably the card you most want access to casting first, since it has a powerful cast trigger (exile an artifact, enchantment, or land) and costs 6G (cheaper than Sire at 7). Additionally, World Breaker can be returned from the graveyard to hand by sacrificing a land, giving it built-in recursion that makes it less necessary to keep safe in exile. Sire of Seven Deaths (7 mana, 7/7 with extensive keywords) is a powerful finisher but harder to cast and has no cast trigger, making it a better candidate to park in exile since you're less likely to want it early. Devourer of Destiny also has a strong cast trigger (exile a colored permanent) and costs 5CC. The imprinted card can be retrieved later with Ugin's Labyrinth's tap ability, so the choice is about which card you're least likely to need soon. World Breaker's cast trigger and graveyard recursion make it one of the more valuable cards to keep in hand rather than exile.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled World Breaker with Ugin's Labyrinth
annotations.betterLine: Exile Sire of Seven Deaths, as it's the most expensive card at 7 mana with no cast trigger, and keep World Breaker in hand for its flexible cast trigger and graveyard recursion ability

annotations.description: Playing a basic Island instead of Scalding Tarn or Urza's Saga is suboptimal. Scalding Tarn would be better because it can fetch any Island or Mountain later, preserving flexibility, while playing it now keeps the option to crack it when needed. More importantly, Urza's Saga is a powerful card that starts accumulating lore counters - playing it now on turn 3 means it gets its chapter I ability ({T}: Add {C}), and next turn gets chapter II (construct token creation). With Lavaspur Boots in hand and Emry as a plan, Urza's Saga is excellent here since it will eventually tutor for Lavaspur Boots (a 1-mana artifact) on chapter III. Playing Island wastes the opportunity to start the Saga clock. The player likely wants to cast Emry (costs {2}{U} but has affinity for artifacts), so playing Urza's Saga now gives {C} mana this turn, and next turn they could play a land + have Saga on chapter II to make constructs. Playing Scalding Tarn now (untapped, crack for Island/Mountain when needed) would also be better than a basic Island since it thins the deck and provides flexibility.

annotations.betterLine: Play Urza's Saga to start the Saga clock, gaining access to colorless mana immediately and working toward tutoring Lavaspur Boots on chapter III. Alternatively, play Scalding Tarn for flexibility.
